title: Ma famille
oneGoal: Students understand that 'famille' means family and can identify their own family members
decisionPoints: How comfortable are students with French sounds?
Do students need visual family photos?
Should I use more gestures for comprehension?
progression: Foundation lesson - introduces core concept
realWorldConnection: Everyone has a family and can talk about who lives at home

title: Qui est dans ma famille?
oneGoal: Students can name 3 basic family members using simple French words
decisionPoints: Are students ready for siblings vocabulary?
Do students need to draw their families first?
Should I include different family structures?
progression: Builds on Lesson 1 by adding more family member words to 'famille'
realWorldConnection: Children can describe who lives in their house

title: Ma famille à moi
oneGoal: Students can point to and name their family members in photos or drawings
decisionPoints: Are students ready for possessive words?
Do some students need help with family photos?
Should I focus on speaking or pointing today?
progression: Builds on Lesson 2 by personalizing family vocabulary with 'my'
realWorldConnection: Children show family photos and talk about them

title: Les familles sont différentes
oneGoal: Students understand that families can look different and that's wonderful
decisionPoints: How can I represent diverse family structures sensitively?
Do students need time to process differences?
Should I focus on similarities or differences today?
progression: Builds on Lesson 3 by expanding understanding that families are diverse and special
realWorldConnection: Families come in many forms - single parents, grandparents, step-families, adopted families

title: Qu'est-ce qu'on fait ensemble?
oneGoal: Students can identify one activity they do with family members
decisionPoints: Are students ready for action words?
Do students need to act out activities?
Should I use family activity photos?
progression: Builds on Lesson 4 by adding what families do together - moving beyond who to what
realWorldConnection: Families eat meals together, play games, watch movies

title: Notre maison
oneGoal: Students can name where their family lives and spends time
decisionPoints: Do students understand home vocabulary?
Should I include apartments and other homes?
Are students ready to describe rooms?
progression: Builds on Lesson 5 by adding where families do activities - connecting actions to places
realWorldConnection: Families live in houses, apartments, different types of homes

title: Nos traditions familiales
oneGoal: Students understand that families have special traditions and celebrations
decisionPoints: How can I include diverse cultural traditions?
Do students need examples of traditions first?
Should I focus on holidays or daily traditions?
progression: Builds on Lesson 6 by exploring special things families do together - traditions
realWorldConnection: Families celebrate birthdays, holidays, have special meals and customs

title: Mon histoire familiale
oneGoal: Students can tell one simple story about their family
decisionPoints: Are students ready to sequence events?
Do students need story prompts or pictures?
Should stories be about recent or past events?
progression: Builds on Lesson 7 by helping students create narratives about their family experiences
realWorldConnection: People tell stories about their families and share memories

title: Je décris ma famille
oneGoal: Students can use simple descriptive words about family members
decisionPoints: Are students ready for descriptive language?
Should I focus on physical or personality traits?
Do students need vocabulary cards for support?
progression: Builds on Lesson 8 by adding descriptive language to make family stories richer
realWorldConnection: When we talk about family, we describe what they look like and how they act

title: Les émotions en famille
oneGoal: Students can express how family makes them feel
decisionPoints: Are students comfortable sharing emotions?
Do students need emotion cards or faces?
Should I include challenging emotions too?
progression: Builds on Lesson 9 by connecting descriptions to feelings about family
realWorldConnection: Families make us feel loved, happy, safe, and sometimes other emotions too

title: Créer notre livre de famille
oneGoal: Students begin creating a simple family book with pictures and words
decisionPoints: Are students ready for a creation project?
Do students need templates or can they start from scratch?
Should I focus on pictures or words today?
progression: Builds on Lesson 10 by having students document their family learning in a book format
realWorldConnection: People create photo albums and books to remember and share family memories

title: Mon arbre généalogique
oneGoal: Students create a simple family tree showing relationships
decisionPoints: Do students understand family relationships?
Should I provide tree templates?
How can I accommodate different family structures?
progression: Builds on Lesson 11 by organizing family information in a visual family tree format
realWorldConnection: Family trees help people understand how family members are related

title: Partager nos familles
oneGoal: Students practice presenting their family information to others
decisionPoints: Are students ready to share publicly?
Do students need presentation supports?
Should sharing be in pairs or small groups?
progression: Builds on Lesson 12 by preparing to share family trees and books with others
realWorldConnection: People enjoy sharing and learning about each other's families

title: Célébration des familles
oneGoal: Students demonstrate their French family vocabulary through presentations and celebration
decisionPoints: Are students confident enough to present?
Should presentations be formal or informal?
How can I ensure every family feels celebrated?
progression: Builds on Lesson 13 by culminating all learning in a family celebration event
realWorldConnection: Communities celebrate diversity and the importance of families

title: Jeux de rôle familiaux
oneGoal: Students practice family vocabulary through dramatic play and role-playing
decisionPoints: Which family scenarios should we act out?
Do students need props or costumes?
Should role-play be structured or free?
progression: Extension - applies all family vocabulary through creative dramatic play
realWorldConnection: Playing family helps children understand family roles and relationships

title: Album photo familial
oneGoal: Students create detailed family photo albums with French captions
decisionPoints: Do students have enough photos to work with?
Should captions be single words or sentences?
How can I help students with writing?
progression: Extension - deepens family book concept with more detailed photo documentation
realWorldConnection: Family photo albums preserve memories and help tell family stories

title: Interviews avec la famille
oneGoal: Students practice asking family members questions in French
decisionPoints: Are students ready for question formation?
Should interviews be homework or in-class practice?
What questions are appropriate for this age?
progression: Extension - uses family vocabulary in authentic communication practice
realWorldConnection: People ask questions to learn more about their family history and members

title: Familles du monde
oneGoal: Students explore how families are similar and different around the world
decisionPoints: Which cultures should we explore?
Do students need visual supports for different cultures?
Should we focus on similarities or differences?
progression: Extension - expands family concept to include global and cultural diversity
realWorldConnection: Families exist in every culture with both universal and unique characteristics

title: Chansons et comptines familiales
oneGoal: Students learn and sing French songs about families
decisionPoints: Which songs are age-appropriate and engaging?
Do students need visual supports for song lyrics?
Should we focus on singing or actions?
progression: Extension - reinforces family vocabulary through music and rhythm
realWorldConnection: Songs and rhymes are traditional ways families share language and culture

title: Exposition des familles
oneGoal: Students create a final exhibition showcasing their family learning and books
decisionPoints: How should we organize the family exhibition?
Should we invite other classes or families?
What format works best for showcasing student work?
progression: Extension - culminates all family learning in a public showcase and celebration
realWorldConnection: Museums and exhibitions help people learn about and celebrate different families and cultures
